newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian army gets orders to shoot after killings.
newsitem.headline: Indian army gets orders to shoot after killings.

text.p: The Indian army was granted sweeping shoot-at-sight powers in the northeastern state of Tripura on Sunday after tribal separatist rebels killed 15 people in two remote villages, a government official said.

"The situation is pretty bad. Shoot-at-sight orders have been issued to contain the violence," Tripura's home minister Samar Chowdhury, speaking from the state capital of Agartala, told Reuters in Calcutta by telephone.
Chowdhury said the army and paramilitary reinforcements had also been given powers to arrest and indefinitely detain suspects.

He said state authorities had imposed an indefinite curfew in the Khowai region where Sunday's killings of 15 Bengali settlers by separatists belonging to the All Tripura Tiger Force occurred. The Sunday attack was the third in the Khowai area in the past week. Last Sunday the tribal separatists set fire to more than 60 houses in ethnic clashes. On Monday they killed 17 people.
